source.title: Minimum sharpness: Scale-invariant parameter-robustness of neural networks
source.authors: Hikaru Ibayashi; Takuo Hamaguchi; M. Imaizumi

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Measures minimum sharpness and normalized sharpness against train–test accuracy gaps on partially randomized MNIST labels, using a different sharpness measure than the claim versions specify.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a correlation experiment on label-randomization ratios and a LeNet replication in Appendix E. The paper describes results in figures, but the supplied text does not give numerical coordinates; no exact values are inferred. Other reported experiments compare Hessian calculation accuracy and efficiency, which do not bear on the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The experiments correlate Hessian-based minimum and normalized sharpness with generalization gaps. They do not measure V7's tolerance to magnitude-scaled weight perturbations before training error rises, or its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. No own result tests another listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that minimum sharpness correlates with generalization gaps at roughly the same level as normalized sharpness in the FCNN and LeNet experiments. This is a qualitative empirical conclusion, without numerical correlation coefficients in the supplied text.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates correlation between sharpness measures and train–test accuracy gaps on partially randomized MNIST labels; it does not test the original claim's memorization, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, architecture, or model-size comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported correlation experiment varies the label-shuffling ratio from 0.0 to 1.0 and includes FCNN and LeNet architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Across MNIST label-shuffling ratios from 0 to 1, the authors report that minimum sharpness and Tsuzuku normalized sharpness correlate with FCNN generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hessian-based scale-invariant sharpness measures correlate with train–test accuracy gaps across label-corruption conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: The LeNet experiment qualitatively reproduces the reported relationship between these sharpness measures and generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The reported Hessian-based sharpness–gap association also appears in LeNet on partially shuffled MNIST.

record.peer_reviewed: ICML Workshop on Theoretic Foundation, Criticism, and Application Trend of Explainable AI, PMLR 139, 2021
record.problems: The correlation results are presented in figures without numerical values in the supplied text. The study reports correlations, not causal evidence that sharpness changes produce changes in the generalization gap. It uses partially randomized labels and only FCNN and LeNet settings for the correlation experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-bearing results omitted. The Hessian trace calculation accuracy and runtime comparisons in Section 3.1, Figure 1 and Appendices F–H do not measure a version's generalization claim.

untested.parts: Near-perfect random-label fitting together with natural-label held-out accuracy above chance and random-label held-out accuracy at chance; generalization gaps alone do not establish these components.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size, dropout strength, and augmentation.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance versus generalization gap among comparably fitted convolutional networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains figure captions and qualitative descriptions but no readable plot coordinates. The corrected states concern whether rows establish a listed version; they do not deny the authors' reported correlations. Hessian calculation accuracy and runtime results do not test any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of fitting natural versus random labels or their held-out accuracies.
No width sweep beyond interpolation or test-error measurement by width.
No comparison of convolutional versus fully connected test error; LeNet is used only in the sharpness-correlation experiment.
No batch-size comparison of generalization performance.

The paper compares minimum sharpness and normalized sharpness with the generalization gap but does not test magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or compare it with norm- and margin-based measures as specified in this version.

rows.subject: FCNNs
rows.size_stated: Three fully connected layers with 128 hidden dimensions
rows.operation_detail: Measured minimum sharpness and normalized sharpness against the train-accuracy minus test-accuracy gap across partially shuffled label ratios.
rows.measure: Correlation of minimum sharpness with generalization gap; generalization gap is Acctrain − Acctest.
rows.value: Figure 2; authors state that the gap and both measures are successfully correlated.
rows.note: The text reports a successful correlation but the figure's numerical values are not stated in the supplied text.
rows.check: Minimum sharpness is a minimized Hessian trace, not V7's perturbation-tolerance measure. The reported correlation cannot establish V7. Appendix D specifies FCNN hidden dimensions of 128 or 512; restricting the subject to 128 is unsupported by the supplied figure text. The measure description also overlaps R2.

rows.subject: FCNNs
rows.size_stated: Three fully connected layers with 128 hidden dimensions
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized sharpness by Tsuzuku et al. against the train-accuracy minus test-accuracy gap across partially shuffled label ratios.
rows.measure: Correlation of normalized sharpness with generalization gap.
rows.value: Figure 2; authors state that the gap and both measures are successfully correlated.
rows.note: Comparator measure. Numerical correlation values are not stated in the supplied text.
rows.check: Tsuzuku normalized sharpness uses Hessian diagonals and weight terms; the experiment does not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance. Appendix D specifies FCNN hidden dimensions of 128 or 512, rather than only 128.

rows.subject: LeNet
rows.size_stated: Three convolution layers with 6, 16 or 120 channels, 5 kernel size, and one fully connected layer with 84 hidden dimensions
rows.operation_detail: Compared minimum and normalized sharpness with the generalization gap on partially randomized MNIST labels.
rows.measure: Relation between sharpness measures and generalization gap.
rows.value: Figure 4; authors state both measures show roughly the same shape and are perfectly consistent with the FCNN case.
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative description, not numerical values.
rows.check: LeNet supplies a convolutional setting, but both sharpness measures remain different from V7's specified measure. Similar shapes and the authors' qualitative correlation statement cannot establish that version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
